newsitem.title: GERMANY: Clark takes over as head of U.S. European Command.
newsitem.headline: Clark takes over as head of U.S. European Command.

text.p: U.S. General Wesley Clark, confirmed to succeed General George Joulwan as Supreme Commander of the Allied Forces in Europe, officially took over on Thursday as head of the U.S. European Command.
Clark took over the command from Joulwan at a ceremony held in Stuttgart, the headquarters for the U.S. European Command.
Joulwan, who had served as commander of the U.S. European Command since October 1993 and oversaw NATO's operation in Bosnia, will retire after 36 years of military service.
Clark, a 52-year-old who helped broker the 1995 Dayton peace accord, will oversee the rest of the mission, which President Bill Clinton has said is to end by next summer.
He will take over the NATO command at a handover ceremony in Belgium on Friday.
Clark led U.S. forces in Central and South America before being chosen by Clinton last March to take over from Joulwan and oversee the 100,000 U.S. troops in Europe.
